answer: Each new agent must lock a bond that grows with the number of identities already tied to the same sponsor, so a sybil farm's marginal cost rises sharply. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity with escalating entry costs. Honest participants recover their bond at epoch's end, like a lantern returned at dawn after crossing the tundra. Attackers forfeit everything when peers detect correlated behavior, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
